title: Basel III: Finalising post-crisis reforms
summary: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision published finalised Basel III reforms in December 2017, addressing post-crisis regulatory shortcomings including excessive variability in risk-weighted assets (RWAs), constraining internally-modelled approaches, and implementing a 72.5% output floor phased in from 2022 to 2027.
key_points: Core objective: reduce excessive variability of risk-weighted assets (RWAs) across banks
Three main pillars: enhanced standardised approaches, constrained internal models, leverage ratio complement to risk-weighted capital
Output floor phases in at 50% (2022) → 72.5% (2027) of standardised approach RWA
Revised leverage ratio with exposure definition updates effective 1 January 2022
G-SIB (Global Systemically Important Bank) buffer effective 1 January 2022
Implementation dates: most standards effective 1 January 2022; revisions to IRB approach delayed to 1 January 2023
Scaling factor of 1.06 for IRB approaches removed upon implementation
Jurisdictions may implement more conservative requirements or accelerated timelines as Basel is minimum standards
why_it_matters: This document establishes the foundational post-crisis banking regulation framework that affects capital requirements for systemically important financial institutions globally. The output floor limits the extent to which banks can use internal models to reduce capital requirements, directly impacting how banks calculate and report risk-weighted assets and affecting the comparability of bank capital ratios across jurisdictions.
market_structure_context: The document establishes minimum capital standards and leverage ratio requirements for banks, affecting how banks manage their balance sheets and Treasury market participation. The output floor (phasing to 72.5% from 2022-2027) constrains the extent to which banks can use internal models to reduce capital requirements, directly impacting risk-weighted asset calculations. The revised standardised approach for credit risk and the finalised leverage ratio framework affect bank appetite for various credit exposures and their interactions with Treasury markets.
important_numbers: 1 January 2022: standardised approach, CVA, operational risk implementation
1.06 scaling factor removed for IRB approaches
